newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on shortcovering, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on shortcovering, soybeans.

text.p: Shortcovering and spillover strength from a rally in CBOT soybeans propelled KCBT hard red winter wheat futures to settle broadly higher.
KCBT traders chalked up part of Wednesday's rally in wheat to shortcovering brought on by signals that the market had become technically oversold.
"I think what you saw today was a shortcovering rally after several hard, down days," a KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat also saw fund-related support, with Refco buying four million July bushels in the session's first half.

CBOT soybeans posted double-digit gains after U.S. analyst Willard Sparks told Reuters in an interview that old-crop soybean prices would be forced up in a similar way as corn prices were last year due to tight supplies.
KCBT wheat also received late support after the release of a survey that estimated Oklahoma's wheat crop would be cut by 40.9 percent because of damage from a freeze earlier in April.
KCBT wheat settled up 4-1/2 to 14-1/4 cents, with new-crop July 14-1/4 cents higher at $4.54-1/4 per bushel. May gained 4-1/2 cents to settle at $4.57.
May lagged new-crop contracts after an unexpectedly high amount of wheat was posted for delivery on Wednesday, the first notice day for deliveries against KCBT May wheat.
Other featured players besides Refco included E. D. & F. Man International, which sold 1.4 million July and bull-spread 900,000 May/July bushels at between six and 10 cents.
